action: 1984 customers: watch the company's own channels for restoration; the company says email and DNS come back first, then other services once it is satisfied that customer data and systems are secure.
date_note: Iceland Review (21 Nov) says the shutdown was on Friday, 20 November.
exec: An Icelandic hosting provider shut down website, email and DNS services used by thousands of customers after what it calls a major attack.
geo_basis: country (company location not stated in the source)
plain: Icelandic web host 1984 shut down its services on Friday after what its managing director called a large and sophisticated cyberattack. Websites, email and DNS for thousands of customers were affected.
summary: Iceland Review reports that web host 1984 shut down its services on Friday after its managing director described a large and sophisticated cyberattack. Website, email and DNS services used by thousands of customers were affected. CERT-IS and the Electronic Communications Office of Iceland are assisting. Investigators have not confirmed who was responsible or whether data were stolen.
title: Icelandic web host 1984 takes services offline after major cyberattack, managing director says

validation.note: Only Iceland Review's page was read. It relays RÚV reporting; the RÚV English page returned no article text to the reader. No statement from 1984, CERT-IS or the Electronic Communications Office was read.

review.note: Title, summary, services, CERT-IS/ECOI assistance, unconfirmed responsibility and Friday shutdown compared with Iceland Review 21 Nov; single_source and severity 2 appropriate
